rationale: Lycopolitan variant of Sahidic ⲕⲱⲧϥ 'pluck, gather'. Distinguished from ⲕⲱⲧⲉ 'surround, encircle'. Confirmed by collocation with ⲃⲓ ⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'carry off fruits'.
Greek loanword προθεσμία 'fixed time-limit, appointed term'. Coptic orthography reflects θ→ⲫ shift. Used eschatologically for the divinely-set span of years from Jesus to Mani's revelation.

Sense uncertain. Context (Pharmouthi/April, harvest, gathering of souls) requires an agricultural-seasonal term. Crum's 'sickness, scab' does not fit. Tentatively 'ripening' or 'change of season'. Open question.
Lycopolitan ϩⲓⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'at/unto the feet of' — directional preposition with personal suffix. Used for arrival into someone's presence, especially of revelatory/salvific descent.

Mani's technical term for the heavenly revelatory Twin/Syzygos who descended to him at age 24 in the year of Ardashir's accession. Distinguished from the Paraclete (=Mani himself) and the Spirit of Truth.
Coptic transliteration of Greek Ἀρταξάρης / Ἀρταξέρξης rendering Middle Persian Ardašīr. Founder of the Sasanian dynasty (224 CE). The historical anchor for Mani's biographical chronology.
Greek Ἀρτάβανος = Parthian Ardawān; the last Arsacid king (Artabanus IV/V), defeated by Ardashir. Marker of Mani's birth period under late Parthian rule.
